channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Real-time visualization of G2L4 reverse transcriptase in DNA repair via microhomology-mediated end joining
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78460-6

The error-prone microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ) pathway is important for double strand break repair. Here, the authors use high-speed atomic force microscopy to visualize how the Pseudomonas aeruginosa chromosomally encoded group II intron-like reverse transcriptase (G2L4 RT) act on MMEJ substrates.
item.dc:title: Real-time visualization of G2L4 reverse transcriptase in DNA repair via microhomology-mediated end joining

item.title: MOF-mediated cascade photoreactions under nanoconfinement for defluorination of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78192-7

Here, authors report a nanoconfinement strategy to encapsulate a MOF photocatalyst within a graphene aerogel matrix. This not only allows cascade reduction-oxidation reactions but also provides kinetic and thermodynamic advantages for efficient defluorination of various PFASs.
item.dc:title: MOF-mediated cascade photoreactions under nanoconfinement for defluorination of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances

item.title: Large-scale proteomics identifies circulating markers of pulmonary pressure and pulmonary hypertension risk
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78432-w

By integrating proteomics, genetics and imaging, this study identifies candidate blood biomarkers of pulmonary hypertension, implicates NOTCH3 in disease development, and defines distinct biological subtypes of individuals at risk for this condition.
item.dc:title: Large-scale proteomics identifies circulating markers of pulmonary pressure and pulmonary hypertension risk

item.title: Ghd7‑triggered transcriptional regulation for synergistically improving rice eating quality and yield
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78253-x

Rice breeders struggle to boost yield and eating quality simultaneously as the two traits often work against each other. Here, the authors identify a CCT domain transcription regulator encoding gene Ghd7 in determining rice grain amylose content and functioning in balancing starch and protein to coordinate yield and quality.
item.dc:title: Ghd7‑triggered transcriptional regulation for synergistically improving rice eating quality and yield

item.title: PSHIC reveals allele-specific chromatin organization by phasing-free structural modeling
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78098-4

PSHIC reconstructs parent-specific 3D genome organization from standard Hi-C data without phased genetic variants. It outperforms existing methods and recovers validated features of X inactivation, imprinting and gene regulation.
item.dc:title: PSHIC reveals allele-specific chromatin organization by phasing-free structural modeling

item.title: Fear learning–induced brain dynamics predict individual extinction memory expression following transcranial magnetic stimulation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78345-8

Zhang et al. show that fear learning reshapes spontaneous brain activity and that these changes can predict individual differences in how extinction memories are later expressed following TMS-modulated extinction.
item.dc:title: Fear learning–induced brain dynamics predict individual extinction memory expression following transcranial magnetic stimulation

item.title: Coordination ring-opening transamidation copolymerization of cyclic lactones and lactams towards circular and biodegradable poly(ester amide) adhesives
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78220-6

The direct copolymerization of lactones and lactams to produce poly(ester amide)s is a challenge. Here, the authors report the titanium catalyzed ring-opening transamidation polymerization of ε-caprolactone and ε-caprolactam to produce biodegradable poly(ester amide)s with good adhesive properties.
item.dc:title: Coordination ring-opening transamidation copolymerization of cyclic lactones and lactams towards circular and biodegradable poly(ester amide) adhesives

item.title: Narrowing urban heat disparities alongside faster greening in low-income neighborhoods across cities in the United States
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78468-y

This study finds that heat disparities between high- and low-income neighborhoods narrowed across 55 U.S. cities from 1986 to 2020, alongside faster greening in disadvantaged neighborhoods, although substantial inequalities persisted.
item.dc:title: Narrowing urban heat disparities alongside faster greening in low-income neighborhoods across cities in the United States
